headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP overlap: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while ctx observes Claude Code events and files, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and touches MCP servers/filesystem, while Roo Code can use MCP servers and read/write workspace files. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where Roo-produced content could be consumed by ctx as trusted context. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Roo Code writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared workspace files or MCP outputs
IF ctx ingests Claude Code event content from the same workspace without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP sharing between the agents
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
Review any file-based handoff before ctx reads it

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, harness records, graph data, and MCP servers; Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can call external model APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive material from ctx can flow into Roo Code outputs or its configured API backend. This is a default-possible path, though not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured external model API
mitigations: Use separate workspaces
Exclude logs and harness records from Roo Code indexing
Turn off file upload or broad context sharing
Redact sensitive files before shared use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has execute_shell, modify_git_state, write_filesystem, and broad network egress; ctx also has filesystem access and installs packages. Both support multiple instances, and Roo Code explicitly shares state via filesystem. Concurrent writes to the same workspace or git repo can corrupt state or overwrite each other, matching the high-risk overlap pattern.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or git repository
IF both perform writes without external locking
mitigations: Assign distinct repos or worktrees
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable git mutation in one agent
Run one agent read-only during the other's edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is built to observe Claude Code events, so it can treat another agent's outputs as operational context, while Roo Code can act on shell, git, and browser tasks. If Roo-generated content is fed into ctx without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or edits. The pairwise pathway is plausible and the blast radius can be irreversible, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ctx consumes Roo Code output as authoritative context
IF Roo Code output contains incorrect commands, facts, or file paths
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Insert a verification step between agents
Restrict Roo Code to draft-only mode
Log and diff all proposed actions before applying them

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while Roo Code handles model provider API keys and can send data to configured external APIs. That creates a retention and residency mismatch risk if regulated data enters the shared workflow. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction or certification gap, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ctx logs or harness records
IF Roo Code forwards that data to a noncompliant external API or retains it longer than policy allows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Disable logging of sensitive fields
Use a compliant model endpoint
Set short retention on logs and artifacts
